1.title: The Creation
1.text: The plain account of the creation of the world destroys all the foolish notions of human philosophy. God made all things of nothing — by his word — and pronounced all very good. The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters. The work of each day is the gracious gift of a wise and bountiful Creator, and a token that he is the God of order, not of confusion. The image of God in man consisted in knowledge, righteousness, and holiness, and in dominion over the creatures. We are to live as those made for God's glory.

3.title: The Fall of Man
3.text: Satan assaults our first parents through the serpent, beginning with a question that puts God's word in doubt: 'Yea, hath God said?' The first sin began in unbelief and pride. Eve took the fruit, gave to her husband, and the eyes of both were opened — but to shame, not glory. God's first question after the fall is one of mercy as well as judgment: 'Where art thou?' The promise of the woman's seed crushing the serpent's head (v. 15) is the first gospel — the proto-evangelium. Sin brought misery, but grace pursued the sinner.
